title: In one lab, four-month-olds kicked more when a kick moved a mobile
summary: Merz and colleagues found that four-month-olds in a laboratory kicked more when an ankle ribbon made an overhead mobile move.
body: Merz and colleagues (2017) ran the mobile task in a laboratory with 42 infants around four months old. A ribbon on an ankle moved an overhead mobile only during learning blocks. Mean kicks per minute were higher in those blocks than in the opening baseline, when kicks did not move the mobile. The authors treated the rise as learning the link in this lab sample. Eight further infants stopped for crying or fatigue and were left out of the analysis.

sources.title: The mobile conjugate reinforcement paradigm in a lab setting
sources.author: Emily C. Merz, Laraine McDonough, Yong Lin Huang, Sophie Foss, Elizabeth Werner, and Catherine Monk
sources.note: Supports the lab result: kick rate during learning blocks exceeded baseline. Developmental Psychobiology 2017;59(5):668-672.
